transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve been feeling more tense and down than I expected lately. I’ve been trying to clean up my image and routine for some arts board stuff, and I’m still doing the basics, but I keep dropping little things I normally care about—like fair planning notes or design drafts. Then I feel guilty and end up canceling plans instead of just catching up.
How long have you been feeling this way—tense and down—since these issues started?
About two months, I think. It started around when I began trying to overhaul my routine and how I present myself.
Do you find that you feel tense or worried even when there isn't a specific reason or task causing it?
I’m not totally sure. I haven’t really noticed it happening out of nowhere—usually I can connect it to something I feel like I should be handling or catching up on.

Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a number of different things in your life, beyond just catching up on tasks—like your performance, relationships, or other responsibilities—more days than not?
I don’t think it’s been that broad. It’s more tied to specific things I feel behind on or worried I’m not handling well. I haven’t noticed myself worrying about everything across the board most days.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual or, on the other hand, feeling restless or fidgety more days than not?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed myself moving slower or being especially fidgety most days.
Have you noticed that you take less pleasure in your usual activities or feel less interested in things you normally enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed a big drop in enjoying things I usually like. Maybe I’ve been a little distracted, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest.
Have you noticed feeling fatigued or lacking energy more days than not, even if you haven’t been particularly active?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get tired sometimes like anyone, but I haven’t noticed feeling worn out or low on energy most days when I haven’t done much.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep—like trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping more than usual—more days than not?
I haven’t really noticed a major change. I might have an off night here and there, but not trouble sleeping more days than not or sleeping way more than usual.
Have you noticed feeling guilty or feeling like you're not good enough, even when things aren't going too badly?

Yeah, a bit. I wouldn’t say I feel worthless or anything, but I do feel guilty. Like since I started trying to clean up my image and routine for the arts board stuff, I’ve been more tense and down than I expected. I’m still doing the basics, but I keep dropping little things I normally care about, like fair planning notes or design drafts, and then I feel bad about it and cancel plans instead of just catching up.
Have you noticed any trouble thinking clearly, concentrating, or making decisions more days than not, even when you're not particularly stressed?
Not really. I mean, if I’m actively stressed about something, I can get distracted, but I haven’t noticed trouble thinking clearly or making decisions most days when nothing much is going on.
Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense anxiety, a racing heart, or a sense that something bad is going to happen out of nowhere?
No, I don’t think so. I get anxious when there’s a clear reason, but I haven’t had sudden episodes out of nowhere with my heart racing or feeling like something terrible is about to happen.

Do you find that your anxiety or worry goes beyond specific tasks or situations and affects multiple areas of your life, like your future, relationships, or performance, even when there isn’t an immediate reason to be concerned?

I’m not really sure it spreads that wide. Most of my worry seems tied to specific things I’m dealing with, not just everything in my life for no reason. I don’t think I’m sitting around worrying about my whole future or all my relationships when nothing is happening.
Do you ever feel anxious or worried even when things are going smoothly and there’s no clear reason to be concerned?

Not really when everything is fine, no. It’s more like since I started trying to clean up my image and my routine for the arts board stuff, I’ve been more tense and kind of down than I expected. I’m still doing the basic things I need to do, but I keep dropping little things I normally care about, like fair planning notes or design drafts, and then I feel guilty and end up canceling plans instead of just catching up.
Do you find that your worrying feels hard to control, even when you're trying to focus on something else?

I’m not totally sure. Sometimes it sticks in my head more than I want it to, but I wouldn’t say it’s completely uncontrollable. If I’m really focused on something else, I can usually shift away from it for a while.
Have you noticed a loss of pleasure or interest in activities that you used to enjoy, even things you normally look forward to?

Yeah, a little. I still care about those things, but I’m not getting into them the way I usually would. Like with the fair planning notes or design drafts, I normally want to work on them, but lately I keep putting them off or dropping them. Then I feel guilty and cancel plans instead of just catching up.
Have you noticed a loss of pleasure or interest in activities outside of fair planning or design work that you used to enjoy, even things you normally look forward to?

A little, yeah. It’s not like I don’t care about anything anymore, but since I started trying to clean up my image and routine for the arts board stuff, I’ve just felt more tense and down than I expected. I’m still doing the basic stuff, but I end up dropping smaller things I normally care about, and then I feel guilty and cancel plans instead of catching up.
Do you find that your mood stays low even when things are going relatively well, or does it seem to improve when there aren’t specific stressors like the arts board tasks weighing on you?

It seems more tied to the stress, honestly. When the arts board stuff or trying to fix my routine and image is hanging over me, I get more tense and down. If that’s not weighing on me as much, I can feel a bit more normal. But lately I’m still doing the basics and then dropping smaller things I usually care about, like the fair notes or design drafts, and then I feel guilty and end up canceling plans instead of catching up.
Have you noticed a loss of pleasure or interest in activities you normally enjoy, even things unrelated to the fair planning or design work, that’s been happening more days than not?

More days than not, yeah, at least lately. It’s tied to trying to clean up my routine and image for the arts board stuff. I’m still doing the basic things, but I keep dropping smaller things I normally care about, like fair notes or design drafts, and then I feel guilty and cancel plans instead of just catching up.
Have you been experiencing little pleasure or interest in activities you used to enjoy—outside of the arts board or design work—nearly every day, even when those stressors aren’t present?

I’m not sure I’d say nearly every day when the stressors aren’t there. I haven’t really tracked it that closely. I do notice it more when that pressure is hanging over me, but outside of that, I can’t say for sure.

Outside of the pressure from the arts board or design work, have you been feeling little pleasure or interest in activities you normally enjoy almost every day, even when those specific stressors aren’t present?
I don’t think I can say it’s almost every day when those specific pressures aren’t there. I haven’t really noticed it that clearly outside of that stress.
